text: Back in Chapter 2 you learned classic file notification mode — a cloud-native subscription so new files are discovered via events instead of repeated directory listing. File Events is the evolution of that same idea, built to remove the two real costs classic notifications always had.

Directory listing is simple to set up but expensive and slow at high file volumes. Classic notifications are efficient, but need elevated permissions and manual lifecycle management — and there's a hard cloud-provider ceiling: 100 jobs on AWS and GCP, 500 on Azure, per storage container. Hit that and you're stuck re-architecting.

File Events eliminates the choice entirely by having a Databricks-managed service own the notification infrastructure. The critical difference: one single queue per external location, not one queue per stream. Many Auto Loader streams share that one queue, which is exactly what sidesteps the per-container cloud ceiling.

Turning it on is one option: cloudFiles.useManagedFileEvents set to true, in a plain Auto Loader stream or added to a cloud_files call inside a Declarative Pipeline. New external locations have File Events enabled by default. It also makes file arrival triggers on Jobs unlimited instead of capped at 10,000 files.
Next lesson: Real-Time Mode for Spark Declarative Pipelines — getting sub-second latency inside the exact same declarative authoring model, without bolting on a second engine like Apache Flink.
